cast/double/malformed-string.reason: SQL CAST reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, so double() over a string column is refused rather than lowered to CAST.

cast/double/negated-malformed-string.reason: The Criteria API has no portable CEL numeric parsing expression that preserves conversion errors under negation.

cast/int/malformed-string.reason: SQL CAST reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, so int() over a string column is refused rather than lowered to CAST.

cast/int/negated-malformed-string.reason: The Criteria API has no portable CEL numeric parsing expression that preserves conversion errors under negation.

cast/int/negative-fraction.reason: int() over a double truncates toward zero in CEL, while PostgreSQL and MySQL CAST round to nearest, so the cast is refused rather than lowered to CAST.

cast/timestamp/malformed-string.reason: timestamp() over createdBy, which is mapped to a String column: a String does not pin an absolute instant, and a malformed value must stay a CEL error, which no SQL cast preserves, so the adapter refuses to compare it.

cast/timestamp/negated-malformed-string.reason: createdBy is stored as a String; timestamp comparisons require an absolute-instant Java column type, rather than lexicographic string ordering or database-specific parsing.

collection/except/as-whole-condition.reason: except is not supported: Cerbos except(list, list) computes a list difference, which has no JPA Criteria translation. Rewrite the policy with a collection macro instead — e.g. size(R.attr.tags.except(["x"])) > 0 is equivalent to R.attr.tags.exists(t, !(t in ["x"])).

collection/except/equals-list-literal.reason: except is not supported: Cerbos except(list, list) computes a list difference, which has no JPA Criteria translation. Rewrite the policy with a collection macro instead — e.g. size(R.attr.tags.except(["x"])) > 0 is equivalent to R.attr.tags.exists(t, !(t in ["x"])).

collection/except/size-of-difference.reason: except is not supported: Cerbos except(list, list) computes a list difference, which has no JPA Criteria translation. Rewrite the policy with a collection macro instead — e.g. size(R.attr.tags.except(["x"])) > 0 is equivalent to R.attr.tags.exists(t, !(t in ["x"])).

collection/filter/as-conjunct.reason: filter() returns a list, not a boolean; only size(filter(...)) has a Criteria meaning, so a filter() conjunct is refused rather than dropped (dropping it would over-grant).

collection/filter/as-whole-condition.reason: filter() returns a list, not a boolean; only size(filter(...)) has a Criteria meaning, so a bare filter() in boolean position is refused.

collection/index/first-element-of-boolea.reason: Positional access into a list of booleans: the same missing index() form as collection/index/first-element-of-number-list, refused in the leaf operand before aBoolList is resolved

collection/index/first-element-of-number.reason: Positional access into a list of numbers. The reference lowers a list attribute only as a JPA collection, a joined table whose rows carry no order a plan can name, so the leaf resolver has no index() form and refuses the operand before the list attribute is resolved. The element's type never comes into it, and neither does the mapping: the corpus maps aNumberList as a related table of element rows, which the membership actions (membership/in/literal-in-resource-number-list, type-mismatch/has-intersection/resource-number-list-against-mixed-literal-list) read and this refusal never reaches

collection/index/first-element-of-object.reason: A positional read of a to-many relation (tags[0].name) has no Criteria form: the relation has no order the adapter can index.

collection/index/first-element-of-string.reason: Positional access into a scalar list. tagNames is a JPA collection and row order in a SQL relation is not defined, so index() has no Criteria form and is refused in the leaf operand
Positional access into a scalar list. tagNames is a JPA collection and row order in a SQL relation is not defined, so index() has no Criteria form and is refused in the leaf operand

collection/index/fractional-position.reason: A relational collection has no declared order for positional indexing.

collection/index/negated-first-element-o.reason: The collection/index/first-element-of-boolean-list read under negation, refused in the same leaf operand below the not

The collection/index/first-element-of-number-list read under negation. The refusal is raised in the leaf operand, below the not, so the negated form throws the same error rather than a NOT around a filter that could readmit a6's null element or an empty list's index error
Positional access into a scalar list. tagNames is a JPA collection and row order in a SQL relation is not defined, so index() has no Criteria form and is refused in the leaf operand

collection/index/negated-out-of-bounds.reason: A relational collection has no declared order for positional indexing.

collection/index/negative-position.reason: A relational collection has no declared order for positional indexing.

collection/map/as-whole-condition.reason: map() translates only as the collection operand of hasIntersection; used as the whole condition it is a list, not a boolean, and is refused.

collection/map/equals-list-literal.reason: map() translates only as the collection operand of hasIntersection, where the projection becomes the inner select of an EXISTS. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list has no Criteria form

hierarchy/descendent-of/empty-delimiter.reason: Cerbos splits a path on an empty delimiter into one segment per character, so the relation is a strict string-prefix test; the reference lowers descendentOf as `LIKE prefix + delimiter + '%'`, which with an empty delimiter also matches the path itself (a2, never its own descendant). The empty delimiter is refused when the hierarchy operand is resolved, before that LIKE is built

principal/except/size-after-removing-res.reason: except is not supported: Cerbos except(list, list) computes a list difference, which has no JPA Criteria translation. Rewrite the policy with a collection macro instead — e.g. size(R.attr.tags.except(["x"])) > 0 is equivalent to R.attr.tags.exists(t, !(t in ["x"])).

principal/exists-one/long-list.reason: exists_one over a literal collection value is not supported. Only exists() and all() can be folded into a flat filter.

principal/exists/list-of-structs.reason: exists first operand must be a variable

regex/matches/compared-to-true.reason: The Criteria API has no portable RE2 regular expression predicate.

regex/matches/end-anchor-before-final-ne.reason: The Criteria API has no portable RE2 regular expression predicate.

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: Bare temporal comparison cannot preserve CEL string equality; use timestamp() explicitly

type-mismatch/equals/boolean-list-elemen.reason: The first disjunct is the collection/index/first-element-of-boolean-list read, refused in its leaf operand before the element's type is compared with the literal 1. The whole condition throws: keeping only the aNumber == 5 branch would agree with this oracle solely because CEL answers the cross-type branch false for every row

type-mismatch/equals/number-list-element.reason: The first disjunct is the collection/index/first-element-of-number-list read, refused in its leaf operand before the element's type is compared with the literal true. The whole condition throws rather than keeping only the aNumber == 5 branch
